# Welcome

::: {.columns style="display:flex; gap:1em;"}
::: {.column width="65%"}

> Welcome to the Societal Needs Data Hub, a central repository for large-scale datasets at the intersection of psychology and society.
<br><br>
The Data Hub’s mission is to bridge psychological science with societal challenges by fostering collaboration across research domains, practitioners, and policy actors, an essential endeavour both in times of crisis and for society’s long-term resilience.
:::
::: {.column width="35%"}
<center>![](logodh.png)</center>
:::
:::

<br> 

# About

The **Societal Needs Data Hub** brings together a growing collection of complementary datasets that offer insight into how people navigate societal challenges, adapt over time, and experience the conditions around them. It offers:

- 📊 **A growing collection of high-quality datasets** 
- 🧠 Documenting **central themes** such as motivation, need satisfaction and frustration, well-being, mental health, trust in institutions, adherence, and risk perception, along with the full catalogue of publications derived from these datasets.
- 🔍 **Comprehensive documentation**, including codebooks, protocols, methodological notes, and variable descriptions  
- 🛡️ **GDPR-compliant controlled access** for sensitive data  
- 🧪 **Synthetic datasets**, tutorials, and reproducible examples for learning and transparent analysis  

[Browse datasets](documentation/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

<br>

# Accessibility and usage of the data

## Layers of accessibility

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## 🔓 Layer 1: Public Access

Openly available to everyone:

- Study documentation and protocols  
- Codebooks and variable lists  
- Aggregated statistics and dashboards  
- Analysis scripts and tutorials  

Use this layer to:

- Explore what the projects are about  
- Understand the structure of the data  
- Teach & learn longitudinal analysis  

[Browse documentation](documentation/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}  

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## 📝 Layer 2: Registered Access

Restricted, de-identified versions of the real data are available **on request**.

To apply, researchers provide:

1. A brief project description  
2. Ethical approval (if applicable)  
3. Required variables/modules  

Approved users sign a **Data Use Agreement**, committing to:

- No re-identification  
- No redistribution  
- Secure storage  
- Proper citation  

Access is granted via **private links** tied to a specific dataset version.

[Request data access](data/download.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## 🔒 Layer 3: Internal Access

Full datasets, including sensitive modules and detailed identifiers, are restricted to the **project consortium**.

These data:

- Are stored in secure private repositories  
- Support ongoing modelling & manuscript preparation  
- Are not shared externally without additional procedures  

:::

## Transparency and reproducibility

All datasets are:

- Released in clearly labeled **versions** (e.g., v1.0, v1.1)  
- Accompanied by **release notes** describing changes in variables, coding, or sample composition  
- Linked to **DOIs** for persistent citation  

Analysis scripts and Quarto documents are aligned with specific data versions, allowing users to reproduce published work and tutorial examples exactly.

## Citation

If you use the resources or data from this hub, please cite the specific dataset(s) and version(s) you relied on.  
An up-to-date citation format for each dataset is available on the [Citation & Acknowledgements](citation.qmd) page.

<br>
